sentences.text: This is Second bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail relating to FIR/Crime No.169/2023 dated 04.06.2023 registered at Police Station Kesali District Sagar, for the offences punishable under Sections 376 and 506 of IPC.
His earlier application was dismissed on merits vide order dated 30.06.2023 passed in
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the case.
He is in custody since 05.06.2023 and trial will take considerable time to conclude.

He further submits that the applicant is a permanent resident of the district and there is no likelihood of his absconding or tampering with prosecution evidence; that the applicant is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by all the directions and conditions which may be imposed by this Court.
On these grounds, the applicant may be released on bail.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 Learned counsel appearing for the State has opposed the bail application.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
This is second application filed on behalf of applicant while the earlier one was dismissed in the light of statements of prosecutrix.
Now, the second bail application has been supported by the learned counsel appearing for the objector/prosecutrix.
The affidavit of prosecutrix is also filed on record.

Looking to the fact that prosecutrix is a major girl of 20 years of age and she is changing her version every now and then and abusing the process of law, the bail application of applicant is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during the pendency of trial.
It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of the Cr.P.C.
Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of.

(ANURADHA SHUKLA) JUDGE rv Sandeep @ Raja Thakur (Gond) vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167353080/
